results.reasoning: Round six, and for the first time nothing gave: all five prior failure modes were re-probed live against a scratch copy and every one held - each mutation names its actor including the defaulted machine username and an env-supplied one, with report matching disk (cli-prior-modes.txt); a combined reply with a refused transition writes nothing, n-0096.yml byte-identical by sha256 across three attempts, why on stderr and exit 2 with stdout empty (cli-refusal-atomicity.txt); empty and whitespace --reply are refused whole, even beside a valid --status and even beside a valid human waive, with no partial write (cli-empty-reply.txt); --json mutations print a change report carrying both ends, the actor and an explicit replies_added while a refused --json keeps stdout empty, and a present-but-empty --actor falls through to the next source with the report agreeing with the ledger on every combination (cli-json-mutation.txt); a reply to a waived or verified thread now reports its own actor - agent, or the visibly-defaulted username - never the status holder, in text and JSON alike, while the bare read still shows 'waived by Probe Human' as the record (cli-reply-to-terminal.txt). New probes of my own found nothing the statement condemns: a combined reply+transition reports one line with both ends, actor and count, a waive-with-reason counts both landed replies as '+2 replies', question-kind flows report identically, a flagless read prints the whole conversation, a mutation aimed at a missing thread refuses on stderr with exit 2, and a set -e loop over three threads stops at the first refusal with the refused thread untouched (cli-round6-probes.txt). Round four's two truthful-but-silent edges remain (an orphan --reason lands nowhere and claims nothing; --waive beside --status reports the move that actually happened) and I concur with rounds four and five that neither violates a statement about reporting the change made. All ten tagged checks pass, and the terminal-reply gap round five named is now itself a tagged check (tagged-checks.txt). Judged by driving the CLI against a disposable copy, not by reading the code.
